applicable_when: The kernel uses a flat 1D grid where each thread computes channel_idx = (flat_offset // 262144) % 64. Since spatial_size=262144 is much larger than any BLOCK_SIZE (128-16384), ALL threads within a single CTA map to the SAME channel. This means the 4 per-channel loads (mean, var, weight, bias) are 4 redundant scalar gathers repeated BLOCK_SIZE times per CTA — each thread issues the same L1TEX address, causing 18/32-byte sector utilization (half the cache line wasted) and 11.8-cycle L1TEX stall per warp. The fix is to compute channel_idx ONCE per CTA as a scalar (pid * BLOCK_SIZE // spatial_size) % C, then do 4 scalar tl.load calls and broadcast to all threads. This eliminates 4 gather loads per thread, replacing them with 4 scalar loads per CTA — a BLOCK_SIZE-fold reduction in L1TEX pressure for channel params. Prior attempts using shared memory preloading crashed due to Triton compilation errors; this approach uses only scalar registers, which is simpler and avoids shared memory entirely.

strategy_title: Shrinking Block Size on Memory-Bound Kernel Causes Regression
strategy_description: Replacing larger autotune configs (512–16384 threads/block) with smaller ones (128–1024) on a memory-bandwidth-bound elementwise kernel caused DRAM throughput to collapse from 85.6% to 33.8% and duration to increase 2.53x. The smaller block sizes inflated the grid from ~2M to ~8.4M CTAs (waves_per_sm jumped from 993 to 3972), massively increasing kernel launch overhead and per-CTA fixed costs without improving memory access efficiency. When a kernel is already near peak DRAM bandwidth, reducing block size does not help coalescing and instead destroys throughput by fragmenting work into too many tiny CTAs.
slow_pseudocode:
# Before: larger block configs, fewer CTAs
autotune configs: BLOCK_SIZE in [512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384]
grid_size = numel // BLOCK_SIZE  # ~2M CTAs
# DRAM throughput: 85.6%, duration: 2.04ms
fast_pseudocode:
# After (regression): smaller block configs, many more CTAs
autotune configs: BLOCK_SIZE in [128, 256, 512, 1024]
grid_size = numel // BLOCK_SIZE  # ~8.4M CTAs
# DRAM throughput: 33.8%, duration: 5.16ms
applicable_when: Never applicable as an optimization — this is a negative pattern to avoid.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel is already near peak DRAM bandwidth (>80% DRAM throughput); kernel is elementwise/memory-bound with high waves_per_sm; reducing block size would multiply grid size by 4x or more. Do not shrink autotune block size range when the baseline is already bandwidth-saturated.
framework_notes: Triton autotune: the selected config determines grid_size = ceil(numel / BLOCK_SIZE). Smaller BLOCK_SIZE → larger grid → more CTA launch overhead and worse memory pipeline utilization on bandwidth-bound kernels. This regression was reproduced twice (iterations 1 and 2) with the same 0.39x speedup, confirming it is a robust anti-pattern.
